steps.title: Read clock angles
steps.content: A clock is 360° around. Each hour mark is 30° apart. The minute hand moves 6° per minute; the hour hand moves 0.5° per minute.
steps.example: At 3:00, the hands are 3 hour marks apart: 3×30° = 90°.

steps.title: Find a right angle
steps.prompt: What is the smaller angle between the hands at exactly 6:00?
steps.explanation: At 6:00 the hands are opposite each other: 6×30° = 180°.

steps.title: Understand odd days
steps.content: A normal year has 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day, so it shifts the weekday by one. A leap year has 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 days, so it shifts by two.
steps.example: If 1 January is Monday, 1 January next year is Tuesday after a normal year.

steps.title: Count the weekday shift
steps.prompt: If 1 January is Monday, what day is 1 January next year after a leap year?
steps.explanation: A leap year shifts the weekday by two days: Monday → Wednesday.

steps.title: Check leap years
steps.content: A year divisible by 4 is normally a leap year. Century years are exceptions: they must also be divisible by 400. Thus 2000 was a leap year, while 1900 was not.
steps.tip: Apply the century exception after checking divisibility by 4.

questions.prompt: How many degrees does the minute hand move in 10 minutes?
questions.explanation: The minute hand moves 6° per minute, so 10×6° = 60°.

questions.prompt: What is the smaller angle at 3:00?
questions.explanation: Three hour marks separate the hands: 3×30° = 90°.

questions.prompt: How many odd days does a normal year contain?
Which century year is a leap year?
questions.explanation: Century years are leap years only when divisible by 400. 2000 is divisible by 400.

questions.prompt: A normal year begins on Friday. On which day does the next year begin?
questions.explanation: A normal year shifts the weekday forward by one: Friday to Saturday.
